info: A decomposition reaction is a chemical reaction in which one compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances. In the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate, heating causes calcium carbonate to form calcium oxide and carbon dioxide gas. The reaction is represented as CaCO3 → CaO + CO2. This is an example of decomposition caused by heat.

questions.questionText: What happens during a decomposition reaction?
options: One compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances
Two elements always form one compound

questions.questionText: What happens to calcium carbonate when it is strongly heated?
options: It decomposes into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide
It forms calcium carbonate and oxygen
It changes only into carbon dioxide
It does not undergo a chemical change
